Adding object-likelihood search order, closed-receptacle awareness, and explicit task pipelines should reduce wasted exploration and improve unseen episodes across task types.

The kettle failure exhausted all 24 steps on unguided, near-alphabetical cabinet exploration. Adding likelihood-ordered search with open-on-arrival, no-revisit rules, and a find-transform-place plan should cut wasted navigation in unseen episodes with tight step budgets.

The failed kettle episode wasted the budget by examining receptacles redundantly (go-to already lists contents), never opening cabinets immediately, and searching without likelihood ordering. The winning lamp episode also spent 6 steps hunting for the lamp after the task was done except for 'use'. This version adds: plan-from-goal-type, open-on-arrival, no-examine-after-go-to, likelihood-ordered search with no revisits, one-object-at-a-time carrying discipline, and budget awareness — all general, none data-specific. Previous rejections likely failed because the guidance was too vague or the gate re-ran identical episodes; these concrete behavioral rules should reduce wasted steps in unseen episodes.
